claims.claim: Fixed-placement feasibility has an exact matching characterization, yielding an XP exact algorithm parameterized by the number k of bugs.
claims.evidence: For a fixed placement, let F_v be the family of nonempty subsets of A(v). A feasible surveillance system is exactly an injective choice S(v)∈F_v, hence exactly a matching saturating the vertex side in the bipartite graph with signature subsets on the other side. Conversely, a saturating matching defines legal monitoring sets M(b)={v:b∈S(v)} because S(v)⊆A(v). There are binomial(n+k−1,k) host multisets and 2^k−1 possible signatures per placement, giving an exact f(k)n^{k+O(1)} decision algorithm, hence XP. The checker independently compared matching with exhaustive signature assignment in 2,424 small fixed-placement cases.
claims.search_method: Direct bidirectional equivalence proof, placement enumeration analysis, and exhaustive small-instance cross-checking.

claims.claim: Regional information bound: for every X⊆V, at least ceil(log2(|X|+1)) bugs must be hosted in N[X]. Moreover, the optimum is additive over connected components.
claims.evidence: Every code of x∈X is a nonempty subset of the h bugs hosted in N[X]. The |X| codes are distinct, so |X|≤2^h−1 and h≥ceil(log2(|X|+1)). Bugs cannot monitor across components, so restricting a global solution proves OPT(G)≥sum_C OPT(C). Conversely, the union of componentwise optima is feasible: bug identities from different components are disjoint, and their nonempty codes cannot coincide. The checker also tested 8,862 feasible small-graph regional cases.
claims.search_method: Direct information-counting proof and both directions of the component decomposition.

claims.claim: If every connected component C has a universal safe house, then OPT is exactly sum_C ceil(log2(|C|+1)), computable in polynomial time.
claims.evidence: Taking X=C in claim 1 gives the lower bound ceil(log2(|C|+1)). If u is universal, placing that many bugs at u makes every nonempty bug subset available at every vertex; there are enough to assign |C| distinct codes. Component additivity gives the stated sum. Components and universal vertices can be found directly in polynomial time. Exact optimization checks passed for stars and cliques through order eight.
claims.witness: For each component C, host k_C=ceil(log2(|C|+1)) bugs at a universal vertex u_C and inject C into the nonempty subsets of those bugs.
claims.search_method: Matching lower bound with an explicit universal-host construction and exact finite checks.

claims.claim: Incidence-capacity lower bound: if rho=max_v |N[v]| and a solution has k bugs, then L(n,k)≤k rho, where L(n,k) is the minimum total cardinality of n distinct nonempty subsets of a k-element set.
claims.evidence: Double counting gives sum_v|S(v)|=sum_b|M(b)|. A bug hosted at z monitors only vertices in N[z], so the latter sum is at most k rho. Since the n signatures are distinct nonempty subsets of the k bugs, their total cardinality is at least L(n,k), proving the inequality. Literal subset-family enumeration independently confirmed the stated layer-minimization principle and L(n,k)≥2n−k in the checked range.
claims.search_method: Exact incidence double count and exhaustive subset-family checks.

claims.claim: The problem is exactly solvable on interval graphs of maximum degree at most two. For every connected component C of order n, OPT(C)=floor(n/2)+1; componentwise summation gives the general answer.
claims.evidence: A connected graph of maximum degree two is a path or cycle. In an interval representation, choosing a cycle interval with minimum right endpoint makes its two cycle neighbors intersect there, so cycles of length at least four have a chord; under maximum degree two only K3 remains, whose optimum is 2. For P_n, claim 3 and L(n,k)≥2n−k give 2n−k≤3k, hence k≥ceil(n/2). If n=2t and k=t, equality forces every bug to monitor a complete three-vertex neighborhood, all k singleton codes to occur, and every other code to be a pair. Cohosted bugs could not have singleton codes, while bugs at adjacent hosts would give the two host vertices the same pair code. Thus the t hosts would have to be distinct nonadjacent internal vertices, but P_{2t} has only t−1 such positions. Hence k≥t+1. The stated odd-vertex construction attains the bound. Exact enumeration of all smaller host multisets confirmed the formula through n=15.
claims.witness: On P_{2t+1}, host bugs at v1,v3,…,v_{2t+1}; give odd vertices singleton codes and each even vertex the pair of its adjacent bugs. On P_{2t}, use v1,v3,…,v_{2t−1} plus v_{2t}, with the analogous codes and a singleton at v_{2t}.
claims.search_method: Structural classification, incidence-equality analysis for even paths, explicit constructions, and exact exhaustive path checks.

claims.claim: Running the source greedy algorithm in both timeline directions and taking the better result is not exact, even on a connected symmetric instance: both runs use seven bugs while OPT=6.
claims.evidence: Using integer-scaled endpoints, the forward source order is L1,L2,L3,L4,L5,L6,U,R6,R4,R5,R3,R1,R2. Exact ComputeSignatures decisions add bugs at processing/host positions (1,2),(2,3),(4,6),(6,7),(9,11),(11,13),(13,13), totaling seven. Reflection gives the identical seven-event trace in the opposite direction. The displayed six-bug codes are legal, nonempty, and pairwise distinct. Moreover, X_L={L1,…,L4} has N[X_L]={L1,…,L6}, while the symmetric right region has the disjoint neighborhood {R1,…,R6}; each region requires three hosted bugs, proving OPT≥6. The checker additionally exhausted all 8,568 host multisets of size at most five.
claims.witness: Take L1=[-2/5,0], L2=[-2/5,1], L3=[3/5,2], L4=[8/5,3], L5=[8/5,4], L6=[13/5,5], U=[7/2,23/2], and Ri as the reflection of Li under x↦15−x. Host a,b,c at L2,L3,L5 and d,e,f at R5,R3,R2. Assign L1,…,L6 codes {a},{a,b},{a,b,c},{b},{b,c},{c}; assign R1,…,R6 codes {f},{e,f},{d,e,f},{e},{d,e},{d}; assign U code {c,d}.
claims.search_method: Exact integer endpoint ordering, direct lexicographic greedy simulation cross-checked by matching, explicit code validation, disjoint regional lower bounds, and exhaustive host-multiset search through five bugs.

target_evidence: The exact target requires either a polynomial-time approximation with ratio strictly below 2 for arbitrary interval families or an appropriate matching inapproximability result. The draft establishes neither. The XP algorithm is not a general polynomial-time algorithm; the exact formulas cover restricted subclasses; the lower bounds do not establish approximation hardness; and the 7-versus-6 example only disproves exactness of bidirectional greedy, not a sub-2 guarantee. These verified results are nevertheless material partial progress. Because the draft explicitly says the general threshold remains unresolved and labels its resolution PARTIAL, its claimed resolution is accurate and not overclaimed.
checks_performed: Read only the designated source-input JSON and baseline-draft JSON; did not use the web, retrieval data, prior runs, receipts, reports, or other solutions.
